stories.title: Activists celebrate as land given protected status
summary: Volunteers say they have been campaigning for 30 years to keep a wild space free from development.

stories.title: Weather warning in place ahead of Storm Boelo
summary: A Met Office weather warning is in place from 18:00 BST on Saturday until 15:00 GMT on Sunday.

stories.title: Birds are more afraid of women than men. Scientists have no idea why
summary: Scientists have uncovered a strange pattern in urban bird behavior: Across five European countries and 37 species, birds consistently fled sooner when approached by women than men.
Researchers have no clear explanation for the difference, raising intriguing questions about how birds recognize and respond to humans.

stories.title: Oxford scientists discover how viruses build themselves without a blueprint
summary: Scientists have captured virus-like particles assembling themselves step by step, revealing how a surprisingly simple process of trial and error produces complex structures with remarkable precision.
The discovery uncovers a crucial molecular turning point that speeds up assembly and could lead to new ways to disrupt viruses and develop vaccines.

stories.title: A revolutionary new microscope could reveal the hidden machinery of life
summary: Researchers have developed a revolutionary microscope that uses an incredibly powerful laser to make previously invisible cellular structures easier to see.
The technology dramatically improves image clarity, allowing scientists to examine small proteins that conventional electron microscopes struggle to capture.
It could eventually reveal how tiny molecular machines interact inside cells, providing an unprecedented look at the hidden workings of life.

stories.title: Honey bees are bullying other bees, scientists discover
summary: Honeybees are aggressively pushing wild pollinators away from flowers, with scientists documenting how they chase off rivals and dominate valuable food sources.
New research warns that rising temperatures and increasing honeybee populations could intensify this competition, threatening wild bees and other important pollinators.

stories.title: Project aims to protect rare arctic-alpine plants
summary: The three year scheme is awarded £65,000 to collect seeds and plant them in the fells.

stories.title: NASA’s Curiosity rover reveals a spectacular new view of Mars with a mystery on the horizon
summary: NASA’s Curiosity rover has revealed a spectacular new view of mysterious, wind-carved cliffs on Mars that may hold evidence of ancient volcanic activity.
With the rover approaching these unusual formations, scientists hope to uncover the secrets behind their strange appearance in 2027.

stories.title: Two storms in two days as Austen and Boelo target UK
summary: The Met Office has named a new storm, Boelo, which is set to bring another round of stormy weather to the UK over the weekend.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising secret behind the human brain’s wrinkles
summary: Scientists have discovered why common marmosets have unusually small, smooth brains despite starting development much like other primates.
The secret lies in subtle changes to brain-building cells that slow neuron production, revealing new clues about how the large, folded human brain evolved.

stories.title: Jackdaw decision 'taken outwith Scotland about Scotland's energy'
summary: Scottish Green Mark Ruskell, the SNP’s Keith Brown and Scottish Labour’s Jenny Young weigh up the Jackdaw decision.

stories.title: Is the UK set to green-light a huge untapped oil field?
summary: Scotland editor James Cook visits Rosebank - the UK's largest known untapped oilfield - in the North Atlantic.

stories.title: NI risks missing 2030 energy goals, says Stormont committee
summary: A committee hears that Northern Ireland could lose out on economic opportunities if action is not accelerated.

stories.title: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
summary: Researchers analyzing nearly 150,000 Reddit posts uncovered unexpected symptom reports linked by users to unapproved versions of retatrutide, including increased appetite, sleep disturbances, and elevated heart rates.
The findings differ from clinical trial results and highlight how AI could help identify potential drug safety signals that warrant further investigation.

stories.title: A rock plunged 90 kilometers into Earth and revealed something unexpected
summary: Scientists discovered a rock in Papua New Guinea that plunged more than 90 kilometers beneath Earth's surface, revealing a bizarre temperature pattern that challenges established theories of Earth's interior.
The unexpected shift from unusually hot to relatively cold conditions could transform our understanding of tectonic plate movements, earthquakes, and volcanoes.

stories.title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands
summary: The research facility in Penrith will also help train the next generation of environmental scientists.

stories.title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut
summary: Frank Rubio is set to be in the crew for the Artemis III mission and previously spent a year in space.

stories.title: Fuel leak which killed fish in River Taff stopped
summary: GE Aerospace previously confirmed fuel got into the river while repair work took place nearby.

stories.title: How Jackdaw ignites row over climate and costs
summary: The UK government approves production from Jackdaw amid intense debate about the project's environmental and economic impact.

stories.title: Will Jackdaw cut your energy bills?
summary: BBC Verify's Ben Chu explains why energy prices are so high, and what Jackdaw could mean for your bills.

stories.title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday
summary: Clear skies permitting, skygazers could be able to spot as many as 10-20 meteors per hour as the shower peaks this week.

stories.title: Burnham defends Jackdaw decision as Badenoch urges PM to overturn ban on new oil and gas licences
summary: The UK government says the field, which is opposed by environmental campaigners, could be producing gas by the end of this month.

stories.title: Too much RNA can starve cells of energy, scientists discover
summary: Scientists have uncovered an unexpected danger lurking inside cells: too much RNA can damage the structures responsible for producing energy.
A new study found that excess RNA, including the normally essential messenger RNA (mRNA), can directly disrupt mitochondria without relying on the immune system.
The discovery could help explain how viral infections and certain aging-related diseases damage cells.

stories.title: A train was delayed by a solar storm. But something didn't add up.
summary: Scientists have cracked a 178-year-old mystery surrounding a train delayed by a solar storm, revealing that the famous incident happened in 1848 rather than 1841.
The discovery rewrites the early history of space weather and highlights a threat that still endangers modern power grids, satellites, and communication systems.

stories.title: Astronauts’ hearts just passed a surprising test for Mars
summary: A new study tracking 13 astronauts suggests that the human heart may be surprisingly well equipped for a journey to Mars, especially with regular exercise during spaceflight.
Researchers found that astronauts' hearts adapted to months of weightlessness and handled simulated Martian gravity without major problems, offering new hope for future missions to the Red Planet.

stories.title: How much gas could Jackdaw provide? And will it cut your energy bills?
summary: BBC Verify looks at what the Jackdaw decision means for bills, energy security and the environment.

stories.title: Astronaut surprise video leaves pupils starstruck
summary: The surprise came after a teacher's father met Peake while working on a cruise ship.

stories.title: Rejuvenation breakthrough: Scientists reverse 60 years of aging in human cells
summary: Scientists have turned blood cells from an 80-year-old into neural stem cells with a molecular age of less than 20, effectively reversing more than 60 years of cellular aging in the laboratory.
The discovery offers a new way to investigate how cells become younger and could help researchers better understand age-related diseases such as Alzheimer's.

stories.title: NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover just shattered the all-time off-world driving record
summary: NASA’s Perseverance rover has shattered a historic space exploration record, traveling farther across another world than any vehicle before it.
Its advanced self-driving system helped it surpass Opportunity’s 28.06-mile record in just five and a half years, a feat that previously took nearly 15.
Now, Perseverance is exploring some of the oldest rocks in the solar system, searching for clues about ancient Martian environments that may once have supported life.

stories.title: A massive asteroid slammed into the North Sea and unleashed a 330-foot tsunami
summary: A decades-long mystery beneath the North Sea has finally been solved.
Scientists have confirmed that the Silverpit Crater, buried 700 meters below the seabed, was created when a 160-meter-wide asteroid struck Earth roughly 43 to 46 million years ago.
The violent collision blasted a towering curtain of rock and water 1.5 kilometers into the air and triggered a tsunami more than 100 meters high.

stories.title: Scientists discover ghostly, eyeless creature hidden in Chinese cave
summary: Deep inside a high-altitude Chinese cave, scientists discovered a ghostly, eyeless freshwater snail that has evolved to live entirely in darkness, marking the first recorded discovery of its kind in China.
Named after a faceless mythical creature, the rare species may already be in danger, with researchers finding only three living adults.
